title: Allocation, mutation and alias-safe numerical work
outcome: Implement a preallocated matrix step, explain ownership and aliasing, and compare semantic results before measuring storage behavior.

exercises.title: Trace a matrix step
exercises.task: Compute the two entries before running the first case.
exercises.hint: Multiply rows by the input, then add bias.

exercises.title: Repeat with new inputs
exercises.answer: Multiplication overwrites both entries before adding the bias.

exercises.title: Debug a width mismatch
exercises.task: Pass a2-by -3 matrix and a length 2 input.
exercises.answer: The declared matrix width must equal input length; validation preserves the previous output here.

exercises.title: Find view overlap
exercises.task: Explain why two different view objects can be unsafe.
exercises.expected: They may address the same parent elements.
exercises.hint: Object identity is weaker than storage independence.
exercises.answer: The rejection uses mightalias, which conservatively checks possible shared storage.

exercises.title: Design scratch ownership
exercises.task: Describe a safe interface for repeated calls that must permit overlapping inputs.
exercises.expected: Use a documented private scratch copy before mutation.
exercises.answer: A scratch buffer can preserve the original input, but its owner and lifetime must be explicit.

exercises.title: Evaluate a speed claim
exercises.task: Explain why fewer measured bytes may not mean faster code.
exercises.expected: Access patterns, dispatch and workload sizes also matter.
exercises.answer: Allocation is one measurement. End-to-end timing and correctness remain necessary.
